question: In a major incident, the hot zone (inner cordon) is where triage and initial treatment of casualties take place.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Correct. The hot zone (incident site) is restricted to specially equipped responders. The warm zone is where triage and initial life-saving treatment occur; the cold zone is the command and treatment area.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Not quite. The hot zone is where the incident itself is — only specially trained and protected personnel enter it. Triage and treatment begin in the warm zone (inner cordon), not the hot zone.
